tier1.notes: Installs in a few seconds from the app, no card removal. Every Bluetooth link this receiver served was running at 27 bytes per radio packet -- the smallest the Bluetooth specification allows. It now asks for 251 on each connection and gets them, confirmed on a radio capture. Traffic reaches the app in roughly a ninth as many radio packets, and writes larger than 20 bytes can now go through instead of having to be split by the sending device -- which is why some Windows machines could not write a licence to a receiver. A sending device whose own Bluetooth adapter refuses large packets will still fail; that is a limit of that adapter, not the receiver. Nothing changes in how the apps talk to the receiver. Includes everything from 0.24.74: the Bluetooth service can no longer be stopped by a connecting device, and the receiver reports a GPS that is powered and listing satellites but hearing none of them, power-cycling it after five minutes to try to recover.

tier2.notes: Write this to the card for the complete release. Your settings do NOT survive a reflash, so you will run first-time setup again -- and that includes the EFB licence, so a re-imaged receiver needs activating again before third-party EFB software will work. Download the .img.xz to a computer and write it to the microSD card with BalenaEtcher. Do not decompress the file first.
